'''Sir John Gordon St Clair Buchanan''' (9 June 1943 – 13 July 2015) was a New Zealand-born scientist and director.

Buchanan was born in [[Auckland]] in June 1943<ref name="BHP CV">{{cite web|url= https://www.bhp.com/-/media/bhp/documents/investors/news/cvjohnbuchanan.pdf?la=en |title=Buchanan, Dr John |publisher=[[BHP]] |accessdate=22 July 2015}}</ref> and grew up in [[Papatoetoe]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rotherham |first1=Fiona |title=Another accolade for 'best connected' businessman |url= http://www.stuff.co.nz/business/industries/6379748/Another-accolade-for-best-connected-businessman |accessdate=22 July 2015 |work=[[The Dominion Post (Wellington)|The Dominion Post]] |date=8 February 2012}}</ref> He received his education at [[Auckland Grammar School]]<ref name="FT obit">{{cite news|url=https://www.ft.com/content/1fea290a-2a43-11e5-8613-e7aedbb7bdb7|title=Sir John Buchanan, scientist and finance chief, 1943–2015|last1=Cramb|first1=Gordon|date=14 July 2015|work=[[Financial Times]]|access-date=22 July 2015 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> and at the [[University of Auckland]] ([[Bachelor of Science|BSc]], [[Master of Science|MSc]], PhD in Chemistry),<ref name="BHP CV" /> and at [[University of Oxford|Oxford]] and [[Harvard University|Harvard Universities]].<ref name="Bloomberg obit">{{cite news |title=John G. S. Buchanan BSc, MSc (Hons 1), Ph.D. |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/people/person.asp?personId=394470&ticker=SN/:LN&previousCapId=256654&previousTitle=BHP |accessdate=22 July 2015 |work=[[Bloomberg Businessweek]] |date=July 2015<!-- ok, it doesn't say that, but it does say that he died on 13 July and the article was accessed on 22 July -->}}</ref> The title of this 1967 doctoral thesis at Auckland University was ''The Clemmensen reduction of 1,4-diketones and diterpenoid transformations''.<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Buchanan |first=John |year=1967 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=The Clemmensen reduction of 1,4-diketones and diterpenoid transformations |publisher=ResearchSpace@Auckland, University of Auckland |hdl=2292/755}}</ref>

Buchanan joined [[BP]] in 1970, where he progressed through the ranks and eventually was appointed by [[John Browne, Baron Browne of Madingley]] as the group's top finance executive, which caused surprise given that his background is in science and not in accountancy.<ref name="FT obit" /> He retired from BP in 2002, as the company has a strict retirement policy set at 60 years.<ref name="FT obit" /> For the next 12 years, Buchanan was with [[BHP]], where he was an independent director (1 February 2003 to July 2015).<ref name="Bloomberg obit" /> He was a director of [[Alliance Boots]] (December 1997 to 2003).<ref name="Bloomberg obit" /> He was deputy chairman of [[Vodafone]] (25 July 2006 to 24 July 2012).<ref name="Bloomberg obit" /> He was chairman of [[ARM Holdings]] (3 May 2012 until 1 May 2014).<ref name="ARM Newsletter">{{cite web|url= https://www.arm.com/company/news/2014/01/appointment-of-new-chairman |title=Appointment of New Chairman |publisher=[[Arm Holdings|ARM]] |accessdate=9 September 2025}}</ref> and a director of [[AstraZeneca]] (25 April 2002 to 29 April 2010).<ref name="Bloomberg obit" />

Buchanan became chairman of [[Smith & Nephew]] in April 2006 and remained in that position until his death. He was chairman of the UK chapter of the [[International Chamber of Commerce]] from May 2008 until his death. Following the [[2011 Christchurch earthquake]], he was founding chairman of the Christchurch Earthquake Appeal Trust UK that he set up with the help of the [[New Zealand High Commission in London]].<ref name="Press EQ charity">{{cite news |last1=Stewart |first1=Ashleigh |title=Expats funnel $6 million into Christchurch rebuild |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/the-press/business/the-rebuild/66162828/Expats-funnel-6-million-into-Christchurch-rebuild |accessdate=22 July 2015 |work=[[The Press]] |date=13 February 2015}}</ref>

In the [[2012 New Year Honours]], Buchanan was knighted for his services to industry.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=60009 |date=31 December 2011 |page=1 |supp=1}}</ref> Buchanan had pancreatic cancer from about 2011.<ref name="Australian obit">{{cite news|url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/business/bhp-director-john-buchanan-dead/news-story/3148ab73b3030c1bd8ad2b4f274c3b0f|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230409105411/https://www.theaustralian.com.au/business/bhp-director-john-buchanan-dead/news-story/3148ab73b3030c1bd8ad2b4f274c3b0f|url-status=live|archive-date=9 April 2023|title=BHP director John Buchanan dead|last1=Chambers|first1=Matt|date=14 July 2015|work=[[The Australian]]|access-date=22 July 2015 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> He became unwell in late 2014 and relinquished some of his roles.<ref name="Press EQ charity" />

Buchanan died on 13 July 2015 and was survived by his wife, son, and daughter.<ref name="FT obit" />
